nodes.label: pointers.py — the pointer audit as a program
nodes.rationale: All six volumes plus the companion as sources and targets at once, in both resolver cases, with the lowercase register NNN hand-grep folded in; answers census classes C1, C2, C3 and C5.

nodes.label: Eight verdicts, four of them findings
nodes.rationale: PARTIAL, PREFIX-ONLY, UNRESOLVED and KIND-MISMATCH are findings; AMBIGUOUS is not, because each volume numbers its own sections.

nodes.label: It never reports UNRESOLVED for a pointer that resolves elsewhere in the roster
nodes.rationale: Four census C1 rows are that case and the text says so each time; the roster is what changes the answer, and both rosters are in the selftest so that is visible.

nodes.label: A range is one claim, not one per number
nodes.rationale: Expanding Registers 1524-1677 into 154 pointers turns one finding about a range into nineteen rows; REGISTER-RANGE is a single site whose verdict states what the sweep covered.

nodes.label: A heading followed by a heading is a contents entry
nodes.rationale: DOCKET.md requires the body occurrence; the rule is asserted in the selftest by line number, because those two line numbers are what it exists to disambiguate.

nodes.label: A labelled proof row is a placement
nodes.rationale: Appendix A states most of its proofs as an indented table, so a heading-only resolver reports nine as unresolved and is wrong nine times.

nodes.label: PREFIX-ONLY is its own verdict
nodes.rationale: The exact-token resolver is in force so the pointer does not resolve, but whether an unheaded parent section is a defect is R3's ruling and not the tool's.

nodes.label: A citation can RESOLVE and still be wrong
nodes.rationale: The audit asks whether an address exists, not what stands at it. Section 34.6 and register 1804 both cite register 1580 for a census that is register 1517's; both score RESOLVED and both send a reader to an entry that does not carry what it was cited for.

nodes.label: --extent lists only the absences something cites
nodes.rationale: An uncited absence is not a pointer failure: 4 cited absences of 133 absences in the extent.

nodes.label: Provenance travels with a lifted function
nodes.rationale: The site patterns are copied from the seated member r2-tools.py and the register patterns and guards from register_cites.py; neither is lifted to r2lib, so the functions carry a provenance comment until they are.

nodes.label: Nothing it reports is new, and the scope is what is
nodes.rationale: Every finding is a DEFECT-CENSUS row or an already-recorded item; what is new is that section 4.6 is cited at 17 sites across three volumes and the 17 PARTIAL ranges were never enumerated.
